title.narrative: Strengthening the Safety and Resilience of Journalists in Sudan Amid Conflict

description.narrative: Background Sudan’s ongoing conflict continues to create one of the most dangerous environments for journalists and media professionals. Beyond direct threats to their safety, journalists face displacement, loss of equipment, digital surveillance, limited access to verified information, and the collapse of professional networks that once supported ethical reporting. The shrinking civic space and targeted attacks on media workers have further weakened public access to credible information at a time when it is most needed. Rationale While traditional interventions have focused primarily on training, there is an urgent need for a holistic ecosystem approach that goes beyond capacity development. Journalists require practical protection mechanisms, safe information ecosystems, psychological resilience, and institutional backing to survive and continue reporting ethically and safely during prolonged conflict. This project addresses those gaps and is fully aligned with UNESCO's Action Plan for Sudan 2025-2027.
